anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Inefficient or incorrect application-level SQL and transaction design that causes the engine to process, move, or lock more data than business logic truly requires.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: Physical corruption or logical inconsistency inside on-disk data pages or index structures that makes storage structures unreliable and forces corrective or fallback behaviour.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly: Insufficient or unstable network, listener, authentication, or socket resources that throttle connection establishment and data transfer between client and server.

When all three root causes co-exist, the system exhibits a blended fault pattern: expensive statements generate very large scans and result sets that traverse damaged pages or mis-linked indexes, triggering error conditions, retries, or full table scans. These bloated operations keep transactions and server backends open for longer, inflating memory use and holding locks while the engine re-reads or re-checks suspect pages. The oversized result sets then contend for limited network bandwidth and connection slots, causing client-side timeouts, increased round-trip latency, rising counts of aborted or half-open sessions, and retry storms. Concurrently, corruption-induced plan fallbacks replace index probes with full scans, further multiplying data volume sent across an already constrained network. Monitoring may therefore show an interleaving of slow-query log explosions, integrity check failures, connection queue buildup, and oscillating throughput that can be mis-attributed to any single layer.

Causally, inefficient workload design amplifies the impact of underlying corruption by touching more pages and indices, increasing the likelihood of encountering bad blocks and forcing expensive recovery or verification paths. Each corruption-triggered retry or full scan magnifies the data transferred, which, in turn, saturates network and connection resources. Network congestion then prolongs transaction lifetimes, raising the window during which further corrupt pages can be read and additional retries spawned. Extended sessions also increase the probability of abrupt client disconnects, and these ungraceful terminations—especially under heavy load—can interrupt in-flight writes, potentially deepening physical corruption. The feedback loop among excessive workload demand, structural corruption, and network exhaustion degrades overall database availability and complicates diagnosis because symptoms at one layer mask or imitate failures in the others.

entry.official_description: INSERT... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE  on a table with more than one UNIQUE KEY is unsafe
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with logical data inconsistency, structural corruption, uniqueness conflicts, or referential-integrity rules being violated by the workload or storage state.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate data consistency, inspect constraints and index integrity, and check whether data-cleaning, repair, or workload correction is required before retrying.
